answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate is acute and non-negotiable. memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor proved reliable on onboarding and invoicing accuracy during the last cycle. However, the assembly line runs at 94% committed volume with zero buffer—any migration risk directly threatens delivery. Verify memory_c2 to confirm vendor capability, then execute a switch but structure it as a phased transition: run parallel supply for 30 days (accept temporary cost premium) to validate their volume scaling under pressure, then shift primary load once proven. This avoids the false choice between cost and risk. memory_c4 shows renegotiation with incumbent recovered margin, but 18% is structural and unlikely recoverable from the current vendor. memory_c6 shows multi-year locks reduce unit cost, but we lack capacity/margin to commit long-term when volumes are constrained. Standard_experiment scale acknowledges the migration hazard while the verification step de-risks the vendor transition.
